18101ca2f93677d5f7554c726f27df60b7fad172: Cortina d'Ampezzo offers 120 km of well-marked runs, a medium-sized ski area that is ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 25 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Cortina d'Ampezzo's DNA is high end: the accommodation, the mountain restaurants and the resort services reflect a clientele that does not count the cost. With a day lift pass at €80, the stay has a price, but the experience lives up to it for anyone who wants to indulge without compromise. With a summit at 2828 m and a village at 1217 m, snow reliability at Cortina d'Ampezzo is generally good from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but conditions recover quickly after the first serious snowfalls. The budget for a stay in Cortina d'Ampezzo is clearly high: €80 for the day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short, Cortina d'Ampezzo is not for everyone, but for those who can afford it, it is probably one of the finest skiing experiences in Europe.

187bbe97a20860a7256b1cabc7fbd48ea2ab6689: Kandersteg is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 13 km of pistes for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Kandersteg's reputation as a family resort is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The moderate altitude of Kandersteg, starting at 1200 m and rising to 1730 m, makes it sensitive to climatic variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. At €42, the day lift pass places Kandersteg among the mid-range resorts on price: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Kandersteg does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
